items.questionAndWhy: Why do baseball umpires' ball-strike calls vary with the count even when pitch location is similar?
items.whatTheyDid: Researchers modeled more than 450,000 MLB pitch calls using Bayesian prior expectations and measures of perceptual uncertainty.
items.whatTheyFound: Count-dependent calls were consistent with Bayesian updating, especially among umpires with greater perceptual uncertainty.
items.whatItMeans: Systematic bias can emerge from rational uncertainty management rather than simple irrationality; mechanism matters before designing correction.
items.streamTitle: MLB umpire count bias fit a Bayesian uncertainty model
items.streamSummary: A large analysis of MLB pitch calls found that count-dependent differences were consistent with Bayesian prior expectations, especially among umpires with greater perceptual uncertainty. The result does not make every biased call optimal, but it shows that systematic judgment shifts can arise from uncertainty-sensitive inference rather than one simple heuristic. Intervention design should target the process actually producing the bias.

items.questionAndWhy: Can six minutes of high-intensity exercise improve executive function in school-aged adolescents?
items.whatTheyDid: Researchers randomly tested a brief HIIT intervention and measured working memory, cognitive flexibility, and inhibitory control.
items.whatTheyFound: Working-memory response speed improved and one flexibility measure was preserved, while inhibitory control did not significantly improve.
items.whatItMeans: Brief exercise may produce selective cognitive effects; a positive finding on one executive function should not be generalized to all cognition.
items.streamTitle: Six minutes of HIIT improved selected executive-function measures, not inhibitory control
items.streamSummary: A randomized study found that a six-minute high-intensity exercise bout improved working-memory response speed and supported one cognitive-flexibility outcome, while inhibitory control did not significantly improve. The mixed result is more informative than a broad 'exercise boosts cognition' claim. Immediate task effects also do not establish lasting academic or behavioral benefit.

items.questionAndWhy: What happens to neural representation when people expect to rely on an external reminder rather than memory?
items.whatTheyDid: Researchers used fMRI to compare remembering, cognitive offloading, and deliberate forgetting conditions.
items.whatTheyFound: Information expected to be externally retrievable became less neurally decodable, resembling the deliberate-forgetting condition in some analyses.
items.whatItMeans: External memory can redistribute internal representation, but reduced decodability is not proof that information was erased.
items.streamTitle: Cognitive offloading made remembered information less neurally decodable
items.streamSummary: An fMRI study found that information participants expected to recover from an external reminder became less decodable in brain activity, resembling deliberate-forgetting conditions in some analyses. The result supports cognitive offloading as a change in how information is maintained, not proof that memory is simply deleted. External support can alter internal representation even when task performance remains adequate.

items.questionAndWhy: Can machine learning and physical spectroscopy together detect large trace-gas emissions missed by human review?
items.whatTheyDid: Researchers combined ML plume detection with physics-based spectroscopic fitting on NASA EMIT imagery.
items.whatTheyFound: The hybrid pipeline detected large emissions with few false positives and suggested at least 25% of large plumes had been missed in earlier human review.
items.whatItMeans: Hybrid AI-plus-physics systems can improve search while retaining a physically interpretable verification stage.
items.streamTitle: A hybrid ML-and-physics pipeline found trace-gas plumes missed by human review
items.streamSummary: Researchers combined machine-learning plume detection with physics-based spectroscopic fitting on EMIT imagery. The system identified large emissions with few false positives and suggested that at least a quarter of large plumes in the evaluated data had been missed by earlier human review. The result is a strong example of using AI for candidate detection while preserving an independent physical verification step.

items.questionAndWhy: How vulnerable are real agent harnesses to adversarial tasks, and does model choice alone determine risk?
items.whatTheyDid: EvoRiskBench tested 450 adversarial tasks across nine model-harness combinations.
items.whatTheyFound: Attack success varied sharply by the model-harness pairing; the most vulnerable tested combination reached 68.44% attack success.
items.whatItMeans: Agent security is a property of the whole execution stack, not the foundation model in isolation.
items.streamTitle: EvoRiskBench found agent security varied sharply by the model–harness combination
items.streamSummary: EvoRiskBench evaluated 450 adversarial tasks across nine model and agent-harness configurations. Attack success differed substantially by the combination, reaching 68.44% for the most vulnerable tested setup. The benchmark does not estimate real-world incident frequency, but it demonstrates that security depends on tool execution, permissions, and orchestration as well as the underlying model.

items.questionAndWhy: Can temporal dependence and higher-order statistics jointly improve causal direction recovery in linear systems?
items.whatTheyDid: Researchers combined two information sources for causal discovery and tested them in simulations and fMRI-related analyses.
items.whatTheyFound: The combined approach improved recovery in tested simulations and increased directional stability in application data under linear acyclic assumptions.
items.whatItMeans: Causal discovery can strengthen directional hypotheses, but its conclusions remain conditional on structural assumptions and data quality.
items.streamTitle: Combining temporal dependence and higher-order statistics improved linear causal discovery in simulations
items.streamSummary: A causal-discovery preprint combined temporal dependence with higher-order statistics and reported improved graph recovery in simulations plus more stable directional results in an fMRI application. The method is promising when its assumptions are plausible, but it does not provide assumption-free causal identification. Linear structure, acyclicity, and measurement quality remain central.

items.questionAndWhy: Was AI actually involved in recent South Korean bank hacks, and what was known at the time?
items.whatTheyDid: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung said AI appeared to have been used in attacks on commercial banks while police and financial regulators investigated.
items.whatTheyFound: AI involvement was an official early assessment; the specific tools, actor, and incremental effect of AI were not yet established publicly on October 6.
items.whatItMeans: Early attribution should preserve uncertainty between confirmed intrusion, suspected AI use, actor identity, and effect.
items.streamTitle: South Korea said AI appeared to have been used in bank hacks, while specifics remained under investigation
items.streamSummary: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung said artificial intelligence appeared to have been used in recent cyberattacks on commercial banks and ordered a rapid investigation. At that stage, the specific AI tools, attacker identity, and extent of compromise were not publicly established. The item is evidence of an official assessment and active investigation, not yet a completed forensic attribution.

items.questionAndWhy: What was known after drones struck merchant ships inside Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone?
items.whatTheyDid: Reuters reported attacks on two vessels in Bulgaria's Black Sea zone, including one sinking, while officials assessed responsibility.
items.whatTheyFound: The attacks and damage were observed, but the drone origin and perpetrator were not independently confirmed at the time.
items.whatItMeans: Maritime-security analysis should separate event confirmation, attribution, strategic intent, and broader escalation claims.
items.streamTitle: Drone attacks on merchant ships in Bulgaria's EEZ were confirmed while attribution remained uncertain
items.streamSummary: Reuters reported two merchant vessels struck by drones in Bulgaria's Black Sea exclusive economic zone, including one that sank. The incidents were confirmed, but responsibility was not independently established at the time; Ukrainian officials blamed Russia while Moscow had not commented. The case illustrates the need to preserve attribution uncertainty even when physical effects are clear.

items.questionAndWhy: Can an LLM help check whether clinical trials follow SPIRIT and CONSORT reporting requirements?
items.whatTheyDid: Researchers developed an element-level automated checker and compared its outputs with human-coded reporting criteria.
items.whatTheyFound: The system reached F1 about 0.822, with document retrieval and locating the right evidence remaining important bottlenecks.
items.whatItMeans: Automated reporting review can support humans, but element-level evidence retrieval and false positives should remain inspectable.
items.streamTitle: An LLM reporting checker reached useful accuracy, with evidence retrieval still a bottleneck
items.streamSummary: A npj Digital Medicine study developed an automated system for checking clinical-trial reports against SPIRIT and CONSORT elements. It achieved F1 around 0.822 in the reported evaluation. The work shows promise for scalable reporting review, but errors in retrieving the relevant passage can propagate into the final judgment. Human review and traceable evidence remain important.
items.attribution: Jiang et al. — npj Digital Medicine

items.questionAndWhy: What can a retraction reveal when published code does not contain the components claimed in the paper?
items.whatTheyDid: A Scientific Reports retraction documented that source code did not implement key claimed security components.
items.whatTheyFound: The mismatch between paper claims and available code undermined reproducibility and the central technical assertions.
items.whatItMeans: Code availability is not enough; reviewers and users need claim-to-implementation traceability.
items.streamTitle: A security paper was retracted after its code lacked claimed core components
items.streamSummary: A Scientific Reports retraction found that the available code did not contain key components described in the paper, including claimed security mechanisms. The case shows that 'code available' is not equivalent to reproducibility. Technical claims need traceable implementation, executable tests, and evidence that the published artifact actually corresponds to the described method.
